title: Three Languages, One Phone, Zero Extra Staff
seoTitle: Three Languages, One Phone, Zero Extra Staff
excerpt: A German message lands at 10:30pm and Mariam doesn't speak German. What she set up instead saved every booking that followed.
seoDescription: October brings guests messaging in English, German and French. See how a two-person tour desk in Khasab covers all three without hiring seasonal staff.

blocks.text: At half past ten one October night, a message landed on Mariam's phone in German: did tomorrow's dolphin trip still have two seats? She does not speak German. By the time she found the right words, the guest had booked the dhow two doors down instead.
The season that arrives in three languages

segments.text: Khasab's dhow and dolphin desks feel this first. Cruise ships return to Port Sultan Qaboos from next month, and Oman's winter tourism season, October through April, is when visitor numbers climb every year. Germany was already Oman's top European source market in the first half of this year, with more than 68,700 visitors, and that count was reached before the cooler months even started, according to
National Centre for Statistics and Information data reported by Oman Observer

. Add guests from the UK, France and further afield who finally book once the heat breaks, and a two-person tour desk starts fielding messages in three or four languages a day, many of them after closing time.

blocks.text: Why a six-week hire never pencils out

segments.text: The obvious fix, hire someone who speaks German or French for the season, rarely survives contact with a small budget. A seasonal, multilingual assistant in Muscat or Musandam typically costs somewhere between OMR 250 and OMR 350 a month, and the rush usually needs coverage for six months, not six weeks. That is OMR 1,500 to OMR 2,100 committed before a single extra booking is guaranteed. What actually solved this for Mariam's desk comes further down this page.

blocks.text: What one slow reply actually costs

segments.text: The real cost was never the hire she didn't make. It was the guest who messaged first and booked with whoever answered first, in a language they could actually read.

blocks.text: A guest who cannot read your reply simply books with whoever answers in a language they understand.

blocks.text: The fix that fits a two-person desk

segments.text: Mariam did not learn German. She pinned the five questions guests ask most, price, pickup point, life jackets, group size and whether dolphins are guaranteed, into one message translated into English, German and French, and saved it as a WhatsApp quick reply for slow moments. For everything else, she turned on
the chat bubble on her website
and let Chatbot.OM read each guest's message and answer back in the same language automatically, day or night, without her typing a single word of German herself.

blocks.text: You do not need to speak the guest's language. You need the answer ready before they ask.

segments.text: Start before the messages start arriving in a language you don't recognise.

items.text: Write down the five questions your desk answers most, in whichever languages last season's guests actually used.
Save those answers as WhatsApp quick replies today, in Arabic, English and whichever third language shows up most in your chats.
Compare the six-month cost of a seasonal hire against a chat tool that replies automatically before you commit to either one.
Track how many messages arrive between 9pm and 6am for one week before the rush starts. That number tells you how badly you need coverage that never sleeps.

blocks.title: Your two-minute check
paragraphs: Open your last fifty WhatsApp chats. Count how many arrived after 9pm, or in a language other than Arabic or English.
If it is more than five, your desk already has a language and timing problem, whether or not it has cost you a booking yet.

items.q: Do I need to reply in perfect German or French?
items.a: No. Guests forgive imperfect grammar. They rarely forgive silence, or an answer that arrives in the wrong language entirely.

items.q: What if my prices change during the season?
items.a: Update your saved quick replies and any chat tool's answers the same day the price changes. An outdated price in the right language is still the wrong price.

items.q: Should I hire seasonal staff instead of using a chat tool?
items.a: For a two to ten person team, work out the six-month cost of a seasonal hire before deciding. Many small tour desks find automatic replies cheaper and faster to set up.

segments.text: October's guests will message in whatever language they think in, at whatever hour suits their body clock, not yours. The fix was never fluency. It was having the right answer ready in the right language before the message arrived.
